pages.text: Phages land on cells at random, so the share of cells hit at a multiplicity of infection MOI is Poisson's 1 − e^(−MOI). An infected cell bursts after its latent period, releasing about a hundred new phages: 1 − e^(−t/τ) of them have burst by time t.
$(thing)Set$(): Phages per cell, Time.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Clumping: the infection varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Too many phages: the cells burst from outside, for nothing.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter runs are faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Cells infected: f = 1 − e^(−MOI)$(br)Cells burst: b = 1 − e^(−t/τ)
